subject: Aurora Cloud marketplace addendum — sequencing & pass-through execution plan
body:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@auroracloud.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Jorge Rivas <jorge.rivas@auroracloud.com>, legal@auroracloud.com
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Aurora marketplace addendum — sequencing & pass-through question

Connor —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our procurement team we need to lock down two things before we can route the addendum through Aurora procurement: (1) who is the invoice owner for marketplace seats (seller vs reseller), and (2) the exact pass-through language for marketplace fees (we have an internal audit window requirement). Attached is a marked-up addendum with our standard marketplace pass-through clause included.

High-level ask: can Redwood accept a limited-pass-through clause that:
- limits reseller liability to amounts invoiced to Aurora (no double recovery),
- adds a 90-day notice period for any audit requests tied to pass-through evidence, and
- requires that any back-charge or clawback be accompanied by an itemized invoice trail.

If that sounds reasonable, procurement wants an execution sequencing plan showing: legal redline owner, ops provisioning owner, and billing owner so they can sign off.

Appreciate a quick confirmation — we are trying to get this executed by the end of next week.

Best,
Elena Morales
Head of Partnerships
Aurora Cloud

-----Original Message Follows-----

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@auroracloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 10:35:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Aurora marketplace addendum — sequencing & pass-through question

Elena —

Thanks for the clear asks and the marked-up addendum. We reviewed quickly, and the team thinks we can get you a proposed execution plan and a set of redlines by EOD Friday. A couple of quick clarifications that will affect the language we propose:

- "Invoice owner": do you need invoice ownership on a per-customer basis (i.e., Aurora invoices end-customers and remits to Redwood) or per-transaction (marketplace seat purchases show seller as invoice owner but Aurora receives a single settlement)?
- "Audit window": 90 days is fine as a baseline, but is Aurora willing to accept an evidence-limited audit (sample-based) for anything older than 12 months? Our finance team prefers that older items be restricted to written attestation + sample artifacts to reduce operational burden.

We'll draft two alternative pass-through clauses: (A) narrow pass-through (Redwood accepts pass-through but caps responsibility to amounts invoiced and requires itemized evidence + 90-day notice), and (B) broader back-charge language (for Aurora internal compliance — higher burden on Aurora to prove entitlements).

Operational sequencing (high-level) we will propose in the plan:
1) Legal redline (Karthik) — finalize pass-through clause and audit mechanics
2) Finance alignment (Laura) — confirm invoice owner and settlement cadence
3) Ops/Provisioning (Connor) — update order form mapping and provisioning sync to reflect invoice owner
4) Execution & DocuSign (Sales ops) — sign and schedule go-live

I'll send the drafted redlines + sequencing matrix (CSV/Excel) by Friday.

Connor O'Brien
Senior Partnerships Manager
Redwood Inference

-----Original Message Follows-----

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Elena Morales <elena.morales@auroracloud.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Aurora marketplace addendum — sequencing & pass-through question

Elena / Connor —

Quick note from legal on the proposed items. We reviewed Aurora's baseline clause in the attachment and have two suggested edits to reduce downstream operational and audit risk for both parties:

1) Liability carve: change the proposed "reseller liable for pass-through amounts" to "reseller liable only to the extent of amounts invoiced and remitted by Aurora to Redwood," and add a requirement that Redwood receives a 30-day cure window prior to any back-charge.

2) Audit scope: we can accept a 90-day audit notice, but propose a tiered evidence approach: for items <=12 months, full document request; for items >12 months and <=24 months, sample-based evidence or attestation; beyond 24 months require written attestation only. This balances Aurora's needs with retained operational cost.

If Aurora legal agrees, we will produce redline language. If Aurora cannot accept tiering, provide alternative language and we will re-evaluate.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference

-----Original Message Follows-----

From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@auroracloud.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Jorge Rivas <jorge.rivas@auroracloud.com>, legal@auroracloud.com
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Aurora marketplace addendum — sequencing & pass-through question

Thanks Karthik —

Tiered evidence is workable. Procurement asked specifically that any cure window not exceed 30 days (reasonable). Aurora also prefers that the invoice owner be Aurora for marketplace seat billing; our accounting team needs to show the seat as sold by an Aurora listing. We can accept a settlement/remittance cadence of 30 days post-invoice.

Next steps from our perspective:
- Redwood to provide the two clause options in redline (A/B) and the sequencing matrix by EOD Monday.
- Once legal and finance are aligned we will generate an internal procurement package and push for signature.

Elena

-----Original Message Follows-----

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Elena Morales <elena.morales@auroracloud.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Aurora marketplace addendum — sequencing & pass-through question

Elena / team —

Finance notes: Aurora as invoice owner is fine but we need to confirm settlement mechanics in the order form. Two asks from Finance:

1) Settlement cadence: 30 days post-invoice is acceptable, but Redwood will require a settlement remittance file with invoice IDs and final gross/fee splits (CSV). The attached matrix includes a sample remittance layout.
2) Failure to remit: we need a practical dispute/cure process — we suggest Redwood hold invoice settlement for the disputed invoice only and rotate with a 30-day cure window before back-charges escalate.

I'll work with Ops to confirm what fields we need in provisioning so revenue recognition matches the marketplace sales.

Laura Bennett
Director, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference

-----Original Message Follows-----

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@auroracloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 16:47:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Aurora marketplace addendum — sequencing & pass-through question

Elena —

Attached are: (1) redline option A (narrow pass-through), (2) redline option B (broader back-charge language), and (3) pass-through sequencing matrix that maps owners and doc links. Links and attachments: DocuSign prep link and a drive folder with the redlines.

Next asks for Aurora: please confirm you accept the tiered audit approach and Aurora-as-invoice-owner + 30-day settlement cadence. If yes, we will prepare the final merged addendum and route to DocuSign.

Attachments: Aurora_Draft_Addendum_v2.docx, Order_Form_ExhibitA_Final.pdf, pass-through_sequencing_matrix.xlsx

Connor O'Brien
Senior Partnerships Manager
Redwood Inference
